newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt paper yields firmer in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: HK govt paper yields firmer in moderate trade.

text.p: Hong Kong government paper yields were up on tighter short-term money and after a weaker close of U.S. treasuries overnight, dealers said on Friday.
"There is moderate selling in the short-end of one- and two-week bills as the short-term cash market is a bit tight on demand for stock runs," a local bank dealer said.
Two stock flotations started their initial public offerings this week and more would come next week, he added.
The yield on one-week notes rose five points to 5.00 percent, three-year notes yielded 6.08 percent against 6.05 and five-year yielded 6.61 percent against 6.58 on Thursday.
The 10-year Hong Kong's Exchange Fund Notes yielded 7.15 percent against 7.14 on Thursday and the seven-year note yield eased to 6.89 percent from 6.87.
Active borrowing were seen on short-dated cash ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
Overnight cash stayed at the high level of 5-5/16 3/8 against 5-7/16 3/8 on Thursday while the three-month was little changed at 5-9/16 1/2.
Dealers said short-term money rates were expected to be steady to firmer from now towards the end of the month. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
